Quick triage notes (10:00 snapshot):
- Concurrency cap: HM-4321 dedicated pool cap hit at 100% for the last ~2.5 hours. Max configured concurrent_requests=8, we've been seeing consistent 8/8.
- Router queue: ingress router queue depth spiked; backpressure triggered but the router backlog isn't draining due to a small set of slow requests.
- Model variant: Marissa confirmed production route is using model-redwood-v2-large (higher GPU time per token). Backup variant model-redwood-v2-medium is certified and has comparable quality for their batch workload.
- KV/prefix cache: hit-rate dropped from 92% -> 58% over the incident window (likely due to increased spread of input prefixes overnight).
- No autoscale events recorded; host pool stable.

Recommended immediate mitigations (ops-safe):
1) Temporarily raise concurrency cap for HM-4321 from 8 -> 12 (small risk of increased tail on other tenants, but will relieve queueing quickly).
2) Shift 20% of batch ingestion traffic to model-redwood-v2-medium (fallback) for 30 minutes to reduce GPU-per-request pressure.
3) Evict oldest entries from KV cache for tenant (force aggressive eviction policy for 10 minutes) to reduce cache thrashing and improve hit-rate.
4) Keep strict per-tenant token/time quotas to avoid noisy neighbor risk.

If you approve, I can execute 1–3 now. Will monitor queue depth and p99 over the next 15m and report. Metrics links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/throughput/horizon-medical?view=overview

-Lauren
